question: What does it mean to be a disciple of Jesus?
answer: A disciple is a learner or apprentice who lives with Jesus and learns from Him how to live. It is more than believing facts about Him; it is trusting Him enough to follow, as when He called the fishermen: "Come, follow Me... and I will make you fishers of people" (Matthew 4:19). We learn from His teaching, His example and His way of life, because "every disciple who is fully trained will become like the teacher" (Luke 6:40).

question: What is the cost of following Jesus?
answer: Jesus never hid the cost. He said, "Anyone who wants to come after Me must say no to themselves, pick up their cross every day, and keep following Me" (Luke 9:23): surrender of our own rule, a daily willingness to lose status, comfort or even life, and steady following. Yet He also promised that "anyone who loses their life because of Me will save it" (Luke 9:24), and Sadhu Sundar Singh found in Christ a peace that the world could neither give nor take away.

question: How do Christians make disciples of others?
answer: Jesus commanded, "Go, then, and make disciples of all the nations" (Matthew 28:19), by baptising and teaching people to obey Him. Paul passed the faith on through generations: "pass on to trustworthy people who will be able to teach others as well" (2 Timothy 2:2). Every believer needs someone further along to learn from and someone behind to help, and discipling is mainly about sharing your life, not having all the answers.
